name: rehearsal
description: See what a database change will actually do to your data, before you do it.

rehearsal.connectionString.markdownDescription: Postgres connection string. Use an environment variable reference such as `${env:DATABASE_URL}` — never paste a password here. Leave empty to read `REHEARSAL_DATABASE_URL` or `DATABASE_URL` from a `.env` file in the workspace root.

rehearsal.envFile.description: Path (relative to the workspace root) of the .env file to read the connection string from.

rehearsal.productionPatterns.description: Case-insensitive regular expressions. If a connection string matches any of them, Rehearsal refuses to connect.

rehearsal.allowedConnections.markdownDescription: Connections that are exempt from production detection, written as `host:port/database`. Adding an entry here is a deliberate act — there is no one-click override.

rehearsal.statementTimeoutMs.description: statement_timeout applied inside every preview transaction.

rehearsal.lockTimeoutMs.description: lock_timeout applied inside every preview transaction. A preview must never be the cause of a lock queue.

rehearsal.sampleSize.description: How many affected rows to show in a before/after sample.

rehearsal.cautionRowThreshold.description: Rows affected above which a statement is marked 'caution'.

rehearsal.destructiveRowThreshold.description: Rows affected above which a statement is marked 'destructive'.

rehearsal.largeTableThreshold.description: Row count above which a table is treated as large for lock and index-build warnings.

rehearsal.explainAnalyze.markdownDescription: Capture a query plan for each UPDATE, DELETE and INSERT. This runs the statement a **second time** inside the same rolled-back transaction, so it roughly doubles how long a preview takes on a large statement. Off by default for that reason.

rehearsal.productionRows.markdownDescription: How many rows each table holds in the database you actually deploy to, as `{"users": 40000000}`. Every count in a preview is exact about the database it measured; given this, each finding also says what the same change costs at the size that matters. Nothing is read from that database — these are numbers you supply.

rehearsal.previewOnSave.description: Re-run the preview when you save a file the Rehearsal panel is already showing. Only that file, and only when a connection is already open — saving never opens one.

rehearsal.mysql.measureOnCopy.markdownDescription:
On MySQL, measure a schema change by **running it against a copy of the table** rather than only by counting. MySQL commits DDL the moment it runs, so there is no transaction to roll one back — a copy is the only way to see what the server really does.

This is the one setting that causes a write. The copy carries a reserved `_rehearsal_clone_` prefix, is never the table you named, is dropped when the measurement finishes, and is swept up on the next connection if a crash left it behind. Your table is never touched.

What it buys: the server's own error — *Incorrect integer value: 'a@b.com' for column 'email' at row 13* — instead of *88 rows cannot convert*. It cannot tell you about foreign key violations, because `CREATE TABLE … LIKE` does not copy foreign keys; the counts remain the authority for those.

rehearsal.mysql.measureOnCopyRowLimit.description: Above this many rows, Rehearsal will not copy a table to measure against — the copy costs more than the better answer is worth, and the counted result is used instead.
